      "observations": [
        "Read the full owned seven-path diff, including all 100 added test lines and the complete 117-line EML fixture. The fixture is a multipart/mixed forward containing a 7-bit message/rfc822 attachment whose own multipart/signed body contains nested multipart data, a base64 text part, a public-key attachment and an armored signature. The raw fixture remains byte-identical at the fixed accepted revision: 5,127 bytes, 117 CRLF line endings, blob 543cf4849f29eaccb54fcca9923592e8e50b3241. Static fixture structure does not prove cryptographic validity.",
        "The signed path strips the application/x-message-display URL parameter, reads the original message once and parses a separate tree. The old code selected a parent boundary and reloaded/extracted between separators. This commit uses the signed part’s own escaped boundary and takes the complete matched multipart substring from the original message data. It keeps parent headers except Content-Type when the parent is not message/rfc822, then adds the signed part headers and preamble. The current accepted source separately trims and normalizes header separators; that later correction is not attributed to this commit.",
        "The encrypted path also reads once and uses getMimeTree with bodies enabled. It now adds the required double-hyphen prefix before each boundary and before the closing delimiter. Nonmatching parts recurse and continue; matching signed or encrypted parts start opening a result without traversing their children again. This is a scoped traversal choice, not a general rule to skip nested content.",
        "Current viewSignedPart takes exec(msgData)?.[0] and concatenates the result without a no-match guard. If that expression has no match, body is undefined and the temporary message string contains the literal undefined. getMimeTree can also return null after a parse exception, while the recursive helper expects subParts. These are explicit static failure paths; no malformed message or parser failure was run.",
        "Both URL-loading helpers change from callbacks to promises. The actual stream listener accumulates binary readBytes strings and resolves at stop without inspecting a stop status. A resolved raw-data promise therefore means the stream callback ran; it does not prove successful transport, parsing, signature verification, or a displayed message. getMimeTree returns null on its caught parsing exception despite the non-null return annotation. Synchronous channel creation/open exceptions occur inside the Promise executor and reject it; later status failures are not converted into rejection by this listener.",
        "The persistent-crypto caller awaits loading before the existing messageParseCallback result. The display caller awaits loading, messageDecryptCb and the completion notification in order. This commit’s composeOpen awaits loading inside its existing try/catch and still falls back with a null tree; the fixed accepted compose caller has later URI and argument simplification. composeStartup does not await composeOpen. The nested-part notification callbacks do not await either view function; they return true to retain the notification. The view functions also do not await msgOpenMessageFromString, so their promise is not a window-open or processing-complete signal.",
        "Ordinary attachment Open and Save remain separate from the Open and Show extraction path. Reuse the existing scoped raw-fetch lesson after checking current fetchAttachment, saveToFile, save and message/rfc822 open. The shared fetch appends outputformat=raw for message attachments or EML filename URLs. Reuse the existing raw-signature-output lesson after checking mimeVerify collection and stop branches; raw exitCode zero is not a verified signature state. No historical attachment-opening or raw-output entry is newly audited.",
        "The extended encrypted-parts task waits for the initial processing event plus a tick, starts the new-window and processing waits before clicking, then directly checks decrypted text, no signed icon and encrypted-ok icon. The new signed-attachment task directly checks outer note text and no signed icon, then inner text, signed-ok icon and absence of encrypted-ok icon after Open and Show. The helpers inspect DOM icon state. They are direct expectations in test code, not fresh cryptographic results. Neither test saves an attachment, compares raw bytes, checks malformed or duplicate boundaries, or exercises loading failure. The inherited negative body assertion has a contradictory positive diagnostic (message text is in body); it predates this patch. All newly added assertions have nonempty messages; missing should alone is not reported as a defect.",
        "Local style and naming: msgURI names the string URI argument, msgData names the raw loaded data, and safeBoundary names the escaped regexp value.
